original_question: Let X be a reflexive Banach space for which the set of equivalence classes of spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences in X is countable. Must X contain a normalized weakly null sequence that generates a spreading model equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact target almost verbatim: it uses the stronger countable version rather than the weaker unique-spreading-model version, assumes X is reflexive, restricts to spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences in X, and asks for the existence of at least one such sequence whose spreading model is equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of some ℓ_p, 1 <= p < infinity.
missing_details: The paper introduces the notation SP_w(X): the class of all spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences in X; the countability hypothesis is specifically that the quotient SP_w(X)/~ is countable.
The equivalence relation ~ is equivalence of basic sequences; a fully stand-alone version should say this explicitly.

To be fully self-contained, the question should define what it means for a sequence (x_n) to generate a spreading model (e_n), using the Brunel-Sucheston asymptotic norm condition stated immediately before Problem 4.

A stand-alone formulation should make clear that the object generated is a normalized basic sequence (a spreading model), and that the comparison with c_0 or ℓ_p is basis-equivalence to their standard unit vector bases.
If one wants complete ambient precision, one may specify the usual Banach-space scalar field convention (real or complex); the paper itself leaves this implicit under standard notation.

The nearby paragraph after Problem 5 gives only a partial positive result under the stronger hereditary hypothesis that SP_w(Y)/~ is countable for every infinite-dimensional subspace Y of X; that hypothesis should not be added to the main question.
refined_question: Let X be a reflexive Banach space. For a normalized weakly null sequence (x_n) in X and a normalized basic sequence (e_n), say that (x_n) generates (e_n) as a spreading model if there exist positive numbers delta_m -> 0 such that for every m in N, every scalars a_1,...,a_m in [-1,1], and every m <= k_1 < ... < k_m, one has | ||sum_{i=1}^m a_i x_{k_i}|| - ||sum_{i=1}^m a_i e_i|| | < delta_m. Let SP_w(X) be the class of all spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences in X, modulo equivalence ~ of basic sequences. If SP_w(X)/~ is countable, must there exist a normalized weakly null sequence in X whose spreading model is equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's Section 5, Problem 5, not Problem 4: the official formulation is the countable-classes version, introduced explicitly as a stronger version of the unique spreading model problem. The draft is already very close to the official wording, so the main repair is to import the immediately preceding definitions of 'generate a spreading model' and of SP_w(X)/~, making the question mathematically stand-alone without broadening it. I did not replace it by the weaker unique-spreading-model question, and I did not add the stronger hereditary hypothesis mentioned only in the subsequent partial-result paragraph.
